summary.title: Introduction to Mitochondria
summary.tldr: Mitochondria are essential organelles in cells, known as the powerhouse of the cell due to their role in producing ATP, the primary energy currency of the cell.

outline.heading: What are Mitochondria?
bullets: Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles.
Found in nearly all eukaryotic cells.
Involved in energy production and metabolism.
Contain their own DNA and ribosomes.
Play a role in cell signaling and apoptosis.

outline.heading: Function of Mitochondria
bullets: Main function is ATP production through cellular respiration.
Convert biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.
Involved in the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation.
Regulate metabolic pathways.
Help maintain cellular homeostasis.

outline.heading: ATP: The Energy Currency
bullets: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate.
Serves as the primary energy carrier in cells.
Energy is released when ATP is hydrolyzed.
Used in various cellular processes, including muscle contraction.
Regenerates from ADP and inorganic phosphate.

outline.heading: Importance of Mitochondria
bullets: Critical for energy metabolism.
Support cellular functions and survival.
Involved in the regulation of the cell cycle.
Impact aging and age-related diseases.
Linked to metabolic disorders.

outline.heading: Mitochondrial DNA
bullets: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA.
Inherited maternally.
Encodes essential proteins for mitochondrial function.
Mutations can lead to mitochondrial diseases.
Used in studies of human evolution and ancestry.

outline.heading: Mitochondrial Dysfunction
bullets: Can lead to a variety of diseases.
Associated with neurodegenerative diseases.
Linked to metabolic syndromes.
Impact on muscle function and energy levels.
Research ongoing for potential therapies.
